record.original_question: Does there exist a constant c such that every unsigned graph G with smallest adjacency eigenvalue at least -3 is c-integrable, meaning there is an integer matrix N such that c(A - floor(λ_min)I) = NN^T where A is the adjacency matrix of G and λ_min is its smallest eigenvalue?

evidence.quote: For a natural number s, G is called s-integrable if there exists an integer matrix N such that s(A − ⌊λmin⌋I) = NNT.
Conjecture 3.15. There exists a constant c such that if G is an unsigned graph with smallest eigenvalue at least −3, then G is c-integrable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple (unsigned) graph with adjacency matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, and let $\lambda_{\min}(G)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue of $A$. For a positive integer $s$, call $G$ $s$-integrable if there exists an integer matrix $N$ (with integer entries, of any size $n \times m$) such that
$$s\bigl(A - \lfloor \lambda_{\min}(G) \rfloor I\bigr) = N N^{\mathsf T}.$$
Determine whether the following holds: there exists an absolute constant $c \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that every finite simple graph $G$ satisfying $\lambda_{\min}(G) \geq -3$ is $c$-integrable.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: it has been proved that there is a constant K such that every connected graph with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 and minimum degree at least K is 2-integrable, and integrability has been established for various subclasses (e.g., strongly regular and sesqui-regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 under valency bounds). No proof for all graphs with λ_min ≥ -3 has appeared.

status_evidence.title: On graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −3 and their lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Connected graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 and sufficiently large minimum degree are shown to be 2-integrable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: 2-integrability holds under a minimum-degree assumption.

status_evidence.title: On the Integrability of Strongly Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Integrability is established for strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 above a valency threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Subclass result supporting but not resolving the general conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress on Graphs with Fixed Smallest Adjacency Eigenvalue: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing integrability conjectures for graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 as ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture is still listed as open in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Sesqui-regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3
status_evidence.snippet: Further partial progress under regularity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Additional partial results in special families.
